BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

**Project Kestrel: Seller draft review against Buyer playbook**

**Note on the Seller's "efficiency note":** The Seller's cover material marks several clauses [STANDARD] and says both sides have "cleared" them. Nothing in the file supports that. Several of those clauses conflict with the playbook, so I have reviewed all 16 items below, not only the [OPEN] ones.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6M. **Reason:** The 20% cap is only available with written authority, which we don't have.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with recovery of the excess only (a true deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Both thresholds are far above playbook and the deductible structure removes recovery of the first AUD 250,000.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion, and any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval. Fundamental claims sit in their own regime (see N-004).
- **Recommendation:** Reject 18 months and the blanket cross-application. **Reason:** The 18-month period has no approval, and the blanket wording would import general limits into other claim categories.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Subjecting title and capacity to general limits is outside the playbook and would leave title risk under-protected.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". No fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct carve-out appears.
- **Buyer wants:** Carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived by anyone.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. **Reason:** The Seller's wording would extend limits to fraud, which the playbook prohibits.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DL 1.1, "every fact... contained or referred to") and public registers (DL 1.2), without limiting specific disclosures.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. **Reason:** Deemed disclosure of the entire data room would defeat warranty claims for matters the Buyer never specifically accepted.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It can never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete clause 8.3. **Reason:** A "discoverable" standard would let the Seller avoid liability for anything in the data room.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence that conditions are met. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6M revenue (~30%).
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make effective consent plus condition evidence a condition precedent. **Reason:** Consent-on-delivery and endeavours wording leave a 30%-revenue customer unprotected.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid (~AUD 3.2M) and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release. Require a payout letter and repayment from Completion funds. **Reason:** Leaving ~AUD 3.2M of secured debt outstanding after Completion exposes the Buyer to the lender's security.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 says on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item, or funded by the Seller. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Require a specific line item or Seller funding, and obtain an on-cost estimate. **Reason:** Omitting the bonuses from the funds flow would leave the Buyer funding them without a price adjustment.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** Broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment and keep the cure. Verify the payment status and obtain a confirmatory assignment. **Reason:** DL 4 confirms transfer is conditional on payment and no receipt is in the data room.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The file does not support the Seller's materiality view or any finding of breach.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Require log preservation, a defined investigation scope and regular written updates. The principal should decide whether a specific indemnity is needed, since that is outside the current playbook positions. **Reason:** The facts are unresolved (possibly ~1,240 records, access unknown), so neither side's conclusion can be relied on yet.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess the contracts (unavoidability, termination rights, accrual) before taking a position. Do not accept "ordinary course" as settled. **Reason:** DL 8 leaves the key characteristics unstated.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to all claims "of any nature" (cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5). Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** Merging all categories under general limits would override the separate title, fraud and tax/IP positions.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012 (DL 10).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal record, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DD-012 as sufficient. Obtain an independent ASIC extract, a PPSR/encumbrance search, and evidence of the Seller's authority to sell. **Reason:** A self-supplied register cannot verify title.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain OPEN. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Mark as OPEN and reject the "settled" characterisation. **Reason:** Nothing in the package resolves tax or IP exposure.

---

**Items for Amelia Frost's decision:**
- Any move to the 20% cap (N-001) or 18-month period (N-003). Neither has been authorised.
- Whether to seek a specific indemnity for the DD-006 incident (N-012).

**Immediate information requests to Seller:** Bluefen consent and conditions evidence; Riverlark payout letter; SOW3 payment records; Sandbar contracts; DD-006 logs and investigation scope; independent title searches; bonus on-cost estimate.
